plan.title: Interventions to increase heat pump adoption in UK homes
plan.question: What interventions are effective at increasing heat pump adoption in UK homes?
scoping_notes: Intervention focus: policies, incentives, advice, financing, regulation, service models or other measures intended to increase heat pump adoption.
Outcome focus: heat pump adoption, installation, uptake, purchase intention or closely related conversion decisions.
screening_criteria: Include UK domestic housing evidence.
Include interventions targeting heat pump adoption or uptake.
Include empirical, evaluation, modelling or policy-analysis evidence.
Include outcomes on adoption, installation, uptake or purchase intention.
Exclude non-domestic buildings.
Exclude documents only about heat pump technical performance.
Exclude documents with no intervention-outcome evidence.
Exclude opinion pieces without evidence or analysis.

component_rationale.group: Included to organise extracted findings by intervention type for a policy-useful synthesis.
component_rationale.select: Included because this is an intervention-effectiveness question, so a subset of relevant documents should be selected for structured extraction.
component_rationale.extract: Included because intervention-outcome findings can be captured in the schema for effects on heat pump adoption.
component_rationale.characterise: Included to map intervention types, evidence coverage, UK relevance and gaps across the corpus.
component_rationale.screen_full: Included because standard depth supports a full-text precision check before synthesis.

assumptions: The review is about interventions intended to increase domestic heat pump adoption, not technical heat pump performance.
UK homes includes owner-occupied, private rented and social housing unless later narrowed.
Adoption includes installation, uptake, purchase intention or conversion from fossil-fuel heating where the source links it to likely uptake.
No publication date limit is imposed unless you request a recency window.
Grey-literature publisher geography is not restricted; UK relevance will be assessed from the document text.
The run may find evaluation evidence, modelling, surveys and policy analyses; only documents with evidence relevant to adoption will be retained.

name: Personal optimism and national pessimism in the UK
question: What evidence is there on the relationship between personal optimism and pessimism about the UK’s national future, and what factors are associated with or may explain this personal-national outlook gap?

plan.title: Personal optimism and national pessimism in the UK
plan.question: What evidence is there on the relationship between personal optimism and pessimism about the UK’s national future, and what factors are associated with or may explain this personal-national outlook gap?
scoping_notes: Concern is the relationship between individual optimism and national pessimism.
Interest includes driving factors or explanations.
User asked for a quick search.
screening_criteria: Include UK-focused evidence.
Include cross-national studies only if UK-specific findings are reported.
Include empirical academic studies and evidence-based reports.
Include evidence measuring personal optimism or related personal outlooks.
Include evidence measuring national pessimism or related societal outlooks.
Include evidence on factors associated with the personal-national outlook gap.
Exclude opinion pieces without empirical evidence.
Exclude sources with no UK-specific findings.

component_rationale.characterise: Included to quickly map how the evidence defines optimism, pessimism and the personal-national outlook gap across sources.
component_rationale.screen_full: Excluded because a landscape analysis does not include the full-text confirmation pass bought by standard or deep analysis.
component_rationale.select: Excluded because the question is not about interventions and their effects, so intervention-outcome document selection is not a good fit.
component_rationale.extract: Excluded because schema-bound intervention-outcome extraction does not fit an associational and explanatory attitudes question.
component_rationale.group: Excluded because there will be no intervention-outcome extraction to organise by intervention, outcome or population.

assumptions: “Individual optimism” means optimism about one’s own life, prospects, wellbeing, finances, or future.
“National pessimism” means pessimism about the UK’s future, society, economy, politics, public services, or national direction.
The review should prioritise UK evidence but may include cross-national studies where UK-specific results are reported.
The question is associational and explanatory, not an intervention-effect question, so structured intervention-outcome extraction is not appropriate.
A quick search means a rapid search pass and a landscape-style synthesis rather than full in-depth document extraction.
No publication-date window was specified, so I have not applied one.

turns.text: Is there a relationship between individual optimism and national pessimism in the UK and what are the driving factors of this?

I can turn this into a standard evidence review plan. I’m treating the question as about UK public attitudes: whether people can be optimistic about their own lives while pessimistic about the country, and what factors are associated with that gap. Because this is an associational/explanatory question rather than an intervention-effect question, I’d include corpus characterisation and a full-text re-screen, but not structured intervention-outcome extraction or grouping.

I’ve revised this to a quick-search version: rapid search effort with landscape analysis. That keeps the focus on finding and mapping the most relevant UK evidence quickly, while flagging if the result set is thin. Because this is still an associational/explanatory public-attitudes question rather than an intervention-effect review, I would include corpus characterisation but not intervention-outcome extraction or grouping. I’ve also removed the full-text re-screen because that is only available at standard or deep analysis depth, not landscape.

name: Quick scan of interventions to reduce childhood obesity
question: What intervention approaches have been studied to prevent or reduce childhood obesity, and what does the evidence base look like across populations, settings and outcomes?

plan.title: Quick scan of interventions to reduce childhood obesity
plan.question: What intervention approaches have been studied to prevent or reduce childhood obesity, and what does the evidence base look like across populations, settings and outcomes?
scoping_notes: Population: children and young people; exact age range not specified.
Intervention focus: approaches to prevent or reduce childhood obesity.
Outcomes: obesity-related outcomes; exact outcome set not specified.
screening_criteria: Include studies of children or young people under 18.
Include interventions aiming to prevent or reduce obesity or excess weight.
Include studies reporting obesity, adiposity, diet or physical activity outcomes.
Include academic studies and policy-relevant grey literature.
Exclude adult-only studies.
Exclude documents with no intervention focus.
Exclude opinion pieces without evidence or evaluation.
Exclude documents not available in English.

component_rationale.characterise: Included to quickly map intervention types, settings, populations, outcomes and obvious evidence gaps across the initial corpus.
component_rationale.screen_full: Excluded because landscape depth does not include the full-text precision re-screen.
component_rationale.select: Excluded because a quick landscape scan will not select documents for in-depth extraction.
component_rationale.extract: Excluded because rapid landscape work will not extract structured intervention-outcome findings from selected documents.
component_rationale.group: Excluded because grouping depends on structured extraction, which is not part of this quick scan.

assumptions: I am treating “childhood” as children and young people under 18 unless you specify a narrower age range.
I am assuming the focus is on interventions intended to prevent or reduce overweight or obesity, not only treatment for severe obesity.
I am not assuming a country or setting restriction; UK-relevant evidence may include international studies and grey literature.
I am assuming outcomes may include BMI, BMI z-score, overweight/obesity prevalence, adiposity measures, diet, physical activity, or related behavioural outcomes.
I am interpreting “quick search” as a rapid landscape scan rather than an in-depth extraction review.

turns.text: I’ve drafted a standard evidence-review plan for the broad question of interventions to prevent or reduce childhood obesity. Because the prompt is broad, I’ve left country, setting, age subgroup, and publication-date restrictions open rather than inventing them. The proposed run uses both academic and grey-literature sources, screens for intervention evaluations, maps the landscape, then extracts structured findings from a selected set of key documents and groups them by intervention type. If you want it narrower, the main levers would be age group, setting, country, or intervention type.

I’ve reworked the plan as a quick scan. This switches from the earlier standard review to rapid search effort and landscape analysis: it will search both academic and grey-literature sources, screen for relevance, classify and appraise the evidence, fetch available full text where possible, and characterise the corpus. It will not do the full-text precision re-screen or structured extraction of intervention-outcome findings, because those belong to a standard or deep intervention review rather than a quick landscape scan. The output should be a fast map of what kinds of childhood-obesity interventions appear in the evidence base, across populations, settings and outcomes, with any thinness flagged.
